text:
morgan: quick sync — coldstart liveness check for int4-long canary showed a weird signal, starting thread to capture notes
kira: saw ~0.8% absolute increase in structured extraction failures vs baseline on the long-doc slice (>=8k tokens)
jamal: ouch. is that on the 1% traffic canary or shadow compare?
kira: 1% live canary, we also had shadow running but the regression is clearer in live sampling
bot-evals: automated report uploaded: https://s3.redwood/tests/1770004444/canary-report.html :robot_face:
yuki: what metric exactly flagged it? mrr/drop or hallucination label?
kira: primary signal was extraction_f1 down by 0.6pp, secondary was human hallucination label up 1.1pp on sampled reviews
pranav: what’s our fallback rule? do we auto-cutover to float16 or do an immediate rollback?
morgan: current policy for onboard int variants: if extraction_f1 drop >0.5pp AND hallucination increase >1pp -> auto-fallback to last stable variant and open incident. This meets both
jamal: confirm: last stable = v2026-03-fp16-2029?
morgan: correct, route -> v2026-03-fp16-2029 on error, and ramp down canary to 0% then pause promos
yuki: should we also enable prefix KV cache bypass for this slice before fallback? might be cache-related for long contexts
pranav: worth trying a quick mitigation (cache bypass), but if human labels already show hallucination, fallback is safer
kira: starting the mitigation run: toggling cache_bypass=true for the 1% canary traffic and re-evaluating 30min sample
bot-evals: mitigation job queued: job_id=canary-mitigation-1770004444-1 status=running
jamal: also add a tighter sampling hook for structured outputs — increase human review rate from 0.1% -> 1% for 30m
morgan: agreed. tagging @ops for potential capacity change if we route to fp16
pranav: reminder of the quick runbook steps: 1) pause ramp 2) run mitigation 3) if metrics don't recover, flip traffic to stable and file postmortem

morgan: runbook snippet for reference:
```
canary_config:
  id: int4-long-2026-03
  traffic: 0.01
  sampling: 0.001
  fallback_criteria:
    - metric: extraction_f1
      delta_threshold: -0.5
    - metric: hallucination_rate
      delta_threshold: 1.0
  fallback_action: route_to:v2026-03-fp16-2029
```

kira: early mitigation results in first 30m: extraction_f1 still down ~0.5pp, hallucination up 0.9pp (so just below auto-trigger on hallucination)
yuki: borderline. since both signals are effectively triggered on business-critical slices, i'd prefer manual flip now rather than risk more user exposures
pranav: +1 manual flip. we can collect more shadow data but user-facing risk is non-trivial
jamal: i'm going to initiate the route change to fp16 now. will post the change id and monitor latency impact (should be small)
bot-evals: traffic routing change submitted: change_id=rt-1770004444-01 -> target=v2026-03-fp16-2029
morgan: thanks. after route switch, schedule a 2-hour observation window and collect extended samples for postmortem
kira: filing a short postmortem template now and attaching the canary report + human review samples
pranav: action items: jamal (route + monitoring), kira (postmortem + sample curation), yuki (assist evals), morgan (notify partners, update runbook)

morgan: one more note — add a new auto-sentinel for "structured-extraction-f1" on long-doc slices so future canaries hit this earlier
yuki: good call. I'll open the sentinel PR after the postmortem

morgan: thanks all :thumbsup:
